food-2-q201.prompt: When a supervisor says only “Follow the rules,” workers skip them without supervision. Which instruction builds understanding?
options: Prohibit questions about reasons and teach only movements.

optionExplanations: This removes the opportunity to understand the purpose.

Helping workers understand the purpose and significance of rules is part of the supervisor’s role.

optionExplanations: Different tasks cannot be substituted by a single completion record.
Procedures everyone can reliably follow are necessary.
Necessary daily and special cleaning are not simple substitutes for each other.
Depending on equipment, distinguish and combine daily cleaning with periodic special cleaning, and provide procedures for each.

food-2-q341.prompt: Production must manage cost and promised timing as well as making good products. Which shop-floor goal reflects QCD?
options: Defective products are acceptable if cost falls.
Produce with a balance of quality, cost and delivery.
Meeting quality alone permits unlimited cost and delivery time.
Meeting delivery permits ignoring quality standards.
food-2-q341.explanation: Production requires appropriate management and balance of quality, cost and delivery.
optionExplanations: Cost reductions do not justify quality nonconformity.
Production requires appropriate management and balance of quality, cost and delivery.

Delivery does not justify abandoning quality or safety standards.

food-2-q169.prompt: A worker who speaks Japanese slowly is always left out of team discussions. What response supports an approachable workplace?
options: Pay attention to each person and create opportunities to listen carefully to this worker too.
Decide slow speakers’ opinions are unnecessary.
Pay no attention unless the worker says something.
Make fun of the worker’s speech at a team meeting.

optionExplanations: Considerate daily communication and attention to individuals build a culture where people can seek advice.
This disregards individuals and discourages consultation.

food-2-q257.prompt: A weight histogram has two peaks, and it combines production data from different raw-material lots. What analysis comes next?

Use only the overall mean to declare both lots identical.

food-2-q348.prompt: A hypothetical machine’s standard speed is 20 units/minute. During 100 minutes of actual running, it runs 40 minutes at 18 units/minute and 60 minutes at 23 units/minute. With no defects, what is the average running speed? No rounding is needed.
options: 2,100 units/minute.
41 units/minute.
21 units/minute.

food-2-q115.prompt: Near-miss forms remain on the supervisor’s desk until month-end, and countermeasures are not communicated. How should this improve?
options: Count submissions without checking content.
Publish a list of reporters’ carelessness.
Do not share reports involving no injury.
Share information promptly and use it to understand hazards and improve the workplace.
food-2-q115.explanation: Share near-miss information early to prevent similar events and accidents.
optionExplanations: Counts alone do not reduce specific hazards.
Emphasize sharing and improvement rather than blame.
Near misses provide information about hazards before accidents occur.
Share near-miss information early to prevent similar events and accidents.

food-2-q379.prompt: A check sheet records pass/fail judgments and measurements. What makes records comparable when the person responsible changes?
options: Change field names daily.
Let each person choose numerical units.
Copy yesterday’s values whenever uncertain.
Specify what is measured, units, judgment criteria and recording methods.
food-2-q379.explanation: Shared measurement targets, units, criteria and methods allow consistent records to be collected.
optionExplanations: Changing field names obscures correspondence between records.
Inconsistent units can cause incorrect comparison and judgment.
Do not copy yesterday’s values when no measurement has been made.
Shared measurement targets, units, criteria and methods allow consistent records to be collected.

food-2-q370.prompt: While compiling product weights, someone proposes discarding out-of-specification values as “probably measurement errors.” What is appropriate before analysis?
options: Always remove maximum and minimum values in every investigation.
Remove all out-of-specification values because only in-specification values are correct.
Check measurement conditions and original records; do not delete values without grounds for exclusion.
Delete outliers until the mean equals the target.

optionExplanations: Being a maximum or minimum alone does not justify exclusion.
Out-of-specification values may be important evidence of actual process conditions.
Correct analysis requires checking data facts and meaning and avoiding arbitrary selection.

food-2-q239.prompt: During an emergency drill, a supervisor tries to restart a dangerous machine to investigate damage. Which decision is appropriate?
options: Prioritize life and prevention of secondary accidents; avoid investigative actions that compromise safety.
Wait to provide first aid until the cause investigation ends.
Stop workers reporting dangers they notice.
Prioritize reenactment over nearby people’s safety to obtain detail.

optionExplanations: In accidents and disasters, put life first and prevent secondary accidents through emergency measures.
Life and necessary first aid take priority over establishing causes.
Do not block information needed to understand site conditions accurately.
Investigations must not create new hazards.

food-2-q087.prompt: After being told “Please inspect it this afternoon if possible,” a worker treats this as an optional suggestion. What should the supervisor change?
options: Stop giving inspection instructions and rely entirely on initiative.
Let the worker infer whether it is an instruction or suggestion from experience.
Clearly instruct it as required work, specifying who is responsible and what must be done.
Only blame the worker publicly for not doing it.
food-2-q087.explanation: Communicate instructions clearly so they can be distinguished from ordinary conversation or consultation.
optionExplanations: Instructions needed to ensure required work cannot be omitted.
Ambiguity causes misunderstanding, so the supervisor must clarify.
Communicate instructions clearly so they can be distinguished from ordinary conversation or consultation.

food-2-q393.prompt: A food company receives conflicting requests from raw-material producers and distributors. Which understanding reflects its relationship with society?
options: Requests from people who never visit the factory do not affect the company.
A raw-material processor is independent of the supply flow.
Supervisors may make promises without regard to company policy.
The company engages with multiple stakeholders, so understand company policy and respond accordingly on the shop floor.
food-2-q393.explanation: Food companies engage with many parties throughout the supply flow and act in line with company policy.
optionExplanations: Trade and consumer requests matter even without direct visits.
Manufacturers are part of the flow from raw-material production through sale and consumption.
Supervisors’ activities must align with company policy.
Food companies engage with many parties throughout the supply flow and act in line with company policy.

food-1-q138.prompt: Unopened processed ingredients were left in a place warmer than specified. Can you judge them to be safe if their best-before date is still in the future?
options: They can always be used if the labeled date is moved one day earlier.

The best-before date applies to unopened food stored under the specified conditions.

food-1-q364.prompt: You are learning the difference between “specified ingredients” and “ingredients equivalent to specified ingredients” in the training material. Which explanation is correct?
options: They are simply categories for domestic and imported products.

They are simply categories for refrigerated and frozen products.

food-1-q223.prompt: In a fictional cooling exercise, the core temperature was 68°C at the start and 23°C when measured later. By how many degrees Celsius did it fall? No rounding is needed.

food-1-q323.prompt: You almost returned a knife used for buckwheat to the storage area for knives used for other ingredients. What should you do to prevent mix-ups?
options: Turn the label over so it cannot be seen.

food-1-q373.prompt: Which combination of processes is listed in the training material as potentially being critical control points?
options: Checking ingredient purchase prices, sales quantities, and delivery costs.

Heat treatment to kill microorganisms, cooling after heating, metal detection, and similar processes.

food-1-q197.prompt: After a worker sets down a hot container, the task is handed over to another person. Which information helps prevent burns?
options: Only the name of the store where the container was bought.

Only the time when the container became empty, with a statement that its temperature need not be checked.

food-1-q313.prompt: When handling chemicals, you expect that they may also get onto your hands and clothing. What is the appropriate approach to protection?
options: All chemicals can be touched with bare hands.

Prevent chemicals from getting onto your hands and body as well as your eyes.

food-1-q093.prompt: A shortcut for a cart carrying ingredients crosses a clean work area. The ingredients are untreated. Which route should you choose?
options: Through the center of the clean area, since the cart does not touch food.

food-1-q348.prompt: During the pre-operation inspection, a lamp that normally lights up does not turn on. What should you do?
options: Attach a picture of a lit lamp and use the machine.
Ignore it because it does not touch the product.
Report the lamp malfunction and have it checked.

Checking that lamps turn on and off normally is also part of the inspection.

food-1-q258.prompt: You are asked to fill in tomorrow’s measurement values on a record sheet in advance. What is the correct response?

Check its function at the start and end of work. A successful end-of-work check alone does not prove that it worked correctly at every moment. If there is a malfunction, report the response concerning products made since the last successful check.

food-1-q083.prompt: After using the adhesive roller before entry, you can still see lint on the underside of your sleeve. What should you do?

Evidence-based critical limits need to be set for each CCP.
Simply changing numbers does not confirm effectiveness or conditions of application.

food-2-q132.prompt: A trial of a new SSOP works under normal conditions, but the required utensils cannot be prepared during busy periods. What should the supervisor decide?
options: Lower hygiene standards without justification only during busy periods.
Review whether the procedure can also be carried out realistically during busy periods, and improve it while maintaining effectiveness.
Require only a check mark in the records during busy periods.
Conclude that there is no operational problem because it works under normal conditions.
food-2-q132.explanation: Whether an SSOP can be carried out realistically even during busy periods is one aspect of its verification.
optionExplanations: Difficulty implementing a procedure cannot be resolved by relaxing standards needed for safety.
Whether an SSOP can be carried out realistically even during busy periods is one aspect of its verification.
Records must not be created for work that was not done.
The procedure must also be feasible in actual busy situations.

food-2-q113.prompt: Two workers have the same number of years of experience but different levels of proficiency in machine operation. How should the supervisor assign work safely?
options: Give them the same duties without checking because their years of experience are equal.
Check each person's skills, abilities, and work-related characteristics before assignment, and provide any necessary advice.
Skip skill checks if the worker wants the assignment.
Assign a worker who is unsure of the operation to work alone to gain familiarity.
food-2-q113.explanation: Appropriate assignment requires understanding each person's abilities and characteristics, as well as years of experience.
optionExplanations: The same years of experience do not necessarily mean the same skills and abilities.
Appropriate assignment requires understanding each person's abilities and characteristics, as well as years of experience.
Willingness alone does not establish the ability to work safely.
An assignment that does not match the worker's skills cannot ensure safety.

food-2-q124.prompt: At the end of work, the tool storage area is disorganized, although the planned production quantity has been achieved. What should the supervisor do before finishing the checks?
options: Skip other checks because the quantity target was met.
Leave it as it is for the next shift to discover.
Check for problems after work and the state of sorting and tidiness, and remove obstacles to the next operation.
Assume disorganized storage is a problem only during production.
food-2-q124.explanation: After work, check equipment and work-related problems, as well as sorting and tidiness that affect the next operation.
optionExplanations: Meeting the quantity target does not mean preparations for the next operation are complete.
The situation needs to be checked before leaving problems for the next shift.
After work, check equipment and work-related problems, as well as sorting and tidiness that affect the next operation.
It affects the safety and smooth progress of the next operation.

food-2-q316.prompt: A team member in charge says, “The SDGs are only about donations outside the company.” Which explanation follows the textbook's approach?
options: Everyday efforts in safety, quality, and production management also contribute to achieving the goals.
The SDGs aim only to increase production quantity.
Reducing food loss in a factory has no connection to the SDGs.
Resource savings achieved by sacrificing safety deserve greater recognition.
food-2-q316.explanation: The textbook explains that the supervisor's basic work and efforts in safety, quality, and production management also contribute to the SDGs.
optionExplanations: The textbook explains that the supervisor's basic work and efforts in safety, quality, and production management also contribute to the SDGs.
The SDGs address multiple social issues, including the environment, human rights, and poverty.
Reducing food loss relates to sustainable production.
Activities that undermine safety are not appropriate sustainability efforts.

food-2-q400.prompt: A hypothetical plan requires 108 kg of acceptable product. If the expected acceptable-product yield relative to raw material input is 90%, what raw material weight is needed? No rounding is needed.
food-2-q400.explanation: Raw material weight × 0.90 = 108 kg, so 108 ÷ 0.90 = 120 kg.
optionExplanations: The yield is not 100%, so raw material weighing the same as the acceptable product is insufficient.
Raw material weight × 0.90 = 108 kg, so 108 ÷ 0.90 = 120 kg.
This is not a calculation that treats 90% as 90 kg and adds it.
108 × 0.90 gives output when 108 kg is input, not the raw material required.

food-2-q354.prompt: At a briefing on food defense measures, it was explained that cameras also help protect workers. Which additional explanation is appropriate?
options: They also help establish facts when incidents occur, and should be used alongside efforts to establish workplace governance.
Camera footage makes raw material management unnecessary.
Footage alone determines the causes of all harm to health.
Installing cameras proves that all workers are dangerous people.
food-2-q354.explanation: The textbook also mentions cameras' role in protecting workers during incidents and stresses the importance of governance.
optionExplanations: The textbook also mentions cameras' role in protecting workers during incidents and stresses the importance of governance.
Cameras cannot replace raw material quality and history management.
Investigating causes also requires information other than footage, testing, and other evidence.
Installation is not grounds for identifying individuals as dangerous people.

food-2-q166.prompt: A subordinate improved a utensil-checking method and reduced mistakes while following the specified hygiene conditions. How should the supervisor encourage this good behavior?
options: Ignore the checking conditions and praise only speed.
Recognize the specific effort and ingenuity, and explain what was good.
Do not mention improvements by anyone other than the supervisor, even when they achieve results.
Simply order the whole team to use the same method, without explaining why the supervisor considers it good.
food-2-q166.explanation: Recognizing and praising effort and ingenuity positively influences the motivation of the person and those around them.
optionExplanations: This does not communicate the value of an improvement that preserves safety and hygiene.
Recognizing and praising effort and ingenuity positively influences the motivation of the person and those around them.
It misses an opportunity to recognize good behavior.
Recognizing and explaining what is good about the improvement helps motivate the person and others.

food-2-q289.prompt: A traceability exercise identified the raw material lot, but it was not possible to retrieve which products used it. What should the supervisor focus on checking?
options: Only the area of the raw material warehouse.
Information linking actual raw material use to product manufacturing records.
Only the color of the raw material delivery vehicle.
Only trends in the product's selling price.
food-2-q289.explanation: Use records must be linked so that product lots can be identified from raw material lots.
optionExplanations: Warehouse size cannot trace the relationship between raw materials and products.
Use records must be linked so that product lots can be identified from raw material lots.
Vehicle color does not show which products used the raw material.
Selling prices alone do not reveal usage history.

food-2-q181.prompt: A diagram of a disinfection process shows only the food before and after treatment. What should be added to understand hazard pathways?
options: Because used solution is discarded, its effects on the surroundings need not be investigated.
Only more photographs of finished products are needed.
Also map prepared disinfectant solution, containers after treatment, used solution, and wastewater.
If the process is called disinfection, the condition of the solution is unrelated to hazards.
food-2-q181.explanation: Processes involve inputs and outputs other than food, such as liquids and containers, which are needed for analysis.
optionExplanations: Waste liquids and vegetable fragments, for example, may be involved in contamination.
Photographs alone cannot fill the gaps in process input and output information.
Processes involve inputs and outputs other than food, such as liquids and containers, which are needed for analysis.
Disinfectant solution also needs to be identified as a process input.

food-2-q325.prompt: The raw materials passed inspection. The person in charge says, “This guarantees the quality of the finished product too.” How should the supervisor explain?
options: Also carry out the necessary inspections and controls during processing and on the product, checking conditions at each stage.
Once raw materials pass inspection, all in-process control becomes unnecessary.
Treat the finished product's sensory inspection as completed when raw materials were received.
If raw materials pass, equipment cannot affect quality.
food-2-q325.explanation: Inspections of raw materials, work in progress, and finished products differ in what they examine and the stage they check.
optionExplanations: Inspections of raw materials, work in progress, and finished products differ in what they examine and the stage they check.
Passing raw material inspection alone cannot guarantee conditions in later processes.
The finished product's aroma, texture, and similar qualities must be checked after manufacture.
Equipment and process conditions can change quality.

food-2-q310.prompt: A particular wear part was out of stock, and the line stopped while waiting for a replacement after a breakdown. What should be established to prevent recurrence?
options: A practice of using substitutes without safety checks.
A simple daily report that omits part names.
A system to manage parts inventory and replacement history and consider replacement timing.
A practice of starting to search for the same part after every breakdown.
food-2-q310.explanation: Manage wear-part inventory and replacement records to support action before breakdowns.
optionExplanations: Unverified substitutes may create equipment, quality, and safety problems.
Without identification, service life and procurement cannot be managed.
Manage wear-part inventory and replacement records to support action before breakdowns.
If parts are unavailable when needed, waiting time will recur.

food-2-q253.prompt: The average weight is on target, but some products are too light and others too heavy. What should be considered when adjusting the equipment?
options: Stop examining equipment precision because the average matches the target.
Remove the minimum and maximum values from the records.
Assume that increasing the setting will always eliminate outliers on both sides.
Investigate causes to reduce variation, rather than looking only at the average.
food-2-q253.explanation: Even if the center is on target, large variation produces out-of-specification items, so precision needs to be improved.
optionExplanations: The average alone does not show whether individual products conform.
Deleting extreme values hides the actual variation.
Raising the average alone may increase the number of overweight products.
Even if the center is on target, large variation produces out-of-specification items, so precision needs to be improved.

food-2-q123.prompt: A supervisor worked only at their own station and was slow to notice an adjacent worker's dangerous posture. How should routine supervision be improved?
options: Limit rounds to checking product quantities.
Collect reports of dangerous postures only at the end of the month.
Continue not checking areas where experienced workers are present.
Arrange opportunities to make rounds and check overall work progress and unsafe conditions.
food-2-q123.explanation: While working, supervisors should also observe the site to check safety and progress, in addition to their own tasks.
optionExplanations: Supervision also checks that work and equipment are in a safe condition.
Daily checks are needed to understand hazards during work.
Unsafe conditions can also arise where experienced workers are present.
While working, supervisors should also observe the site to check safety and progress, in addition to their own tasks.

food-2-q309.prompt: In a hypothetical plan, the operating rate is 80%, and output while running is 90% of the standard speed. Using the same definition, what is the overall equipment efficiency? No rounding is needed.
food-2-q309.explanation: 0.80 × 0.90 × 100 = 72%. Combine the effects of stoppages and speed during operation.
optionExplanations: The average of the two percentages is not the overall efficiency.
0.80 × 0.90 × 100 = 72%. Combine the effects of stoppages and speed during operation.
The difference between the two percentages is not the overall efficiency.
The calculation does not add the two percentages.

food-2-q312.prompt: Waste plastic and metal parts are being put into the same box on the production floor. What instruction should the supervisor give?
options: Flush away only items that can be washed away with cleaning water.
Mix them out of sight to reduce their volume.
Take them to the waste storage area using the specified categories and methods.
Let workers freely take them away without checking the collection destination.
food-2-q312.explanation: Waste must be properly sorted and managed using the specified methods.
optionExplanations: Flushing waste into drains creates problems such as increased treatment load.
Mixing waste does not constitute appropriate disposal.
Waste must be properly sorted and managed using the specified methods.
Taking waste away outside the specified disposal process is inappropriate.

food-2-q140.prompt: A worker misunderstood a correct sign as meaning something else and made an operating error. After also asking what the worker understood, which measure appropriately addresses the misperception?
options: Identify what was misunderstood and draw attention to the correct information.
Change only the operation to fit the incorrect meaning the worker learned.
Treat everyone using the same equipment as lacking skills and start them all over from the beginning.
Make no further checks because the sign was correct.
food-2-q140.explanation: Misperception is an error in which correct information is misunderstood, and drawing attention to it is given as a countermeasure.
optionExplanations: Misperception is an error in which correct information is misunderstood, and drawing attention to it is given as a countermeasure.
This incorporates the misperception into operations without correcting it.
The misunderstanding needs to be identified so that measures match the cause.
Even with a correct sign, the misunderstanding in how it was received must be addressed.

food-2-q148.prompt: A deviation was traced to a faulty temperature control valve. Which statement appropriately relates restoring the temperature to preventing recurrence?
options: Do not stop after restoring the temperature; take action to remove the root cause of the valve fault.
Do nothing to control affected products until the root cause is identified.
Restoring the temperature simultaneously completes the cause investigation and countermeasures.
Changing only the recorded temperature setting constitutes corrective action.
food-2-q148.explanation: Distinguish correction that restores control from corrective action that removes the root cause and prevents recurrence.
optionExplanations: Distinguish correction that restores control from corrective action that removes the root cause and prevents recurrence.
Alongside investigating the cause, action is needed on the process and products affected by the deviation.
The root cause may remain after the condition is simply restored.
Changing records alone cannot remove the actual cause.

food-2-q244.prompt: Products meet specifications, but frequent spills during processing have increased raw material costs. How should quality management be assessed?
options: Depart from product specifications to reduce spills.
Treat raw material loss control as an issue alongside safety and good quality.
Always regard increased raw material costs as solely a sales department problem.
If products pass, regard raw material losses as unrelated to quality management.
food-2-q244.explanation: Quality management aims to ensure safety, good quality, and profits by avoiding waste of raw materials.
optionExplanations: Departing from specifications undermines the supply of good-quality products.
Quality management aims to ensure safety, good quality, and profits by avoiding waste of raw materials.
Losses arising in the manufacturing process are a site management issue.
Producing acceptable products alone does not resolve raw material loss.

food-2-q385.prompt: The actual progress line is gradually moving farther below the planned line. The final delivery deadline is still some time away. What should the supervisor do?
options: Assume changes in slope have no relation to production speed.
Do not examine the gap until the delivery deadline.
Identify the delay trend early, check the causes and outlook, and make adjustments.
Move the planned line to the actual line to erase the delay.
food-2-q385.explanation: Progress control charts help identify delays and slowing production early so that action can be taken.
optionExplanations: The slope of a cumulative line indicates production progress over a given time.
Failing to act early may leave less room for later adjustment.
Progress control charts help identify delays and slowing production early so that action can be taken.
Changing the chart does not resolve the actual delay.

food-2-q218.prompt: A proposed process schedule would select CCPs for a new product first, then investigate product characteristics and hazards. How should the order be corrected?
options: Once monitoring records have been created, hazard analysis can be omitted.
Do not perform any on-site checks until hazard analysis is finished.
Decide the number of CCPs first, then keep only hazards that fit that number.
Analyze hazards using the necessary preparatory information and on-site checks, then determine CCPs from the results.
food-2-q218.explanation: The 12 steps proceed through preparation, hazard analysis, and determination of CCPs in that order.
optionExplanations: Monitoring forms do not replace hazard analysis.
The results of verifying the flow diagram on site are used in hazard analysis.
Fixing the conclusion first may overlook hazards that need to be addressed.
The 12 steps proceed through preparation, hazard analysis, and determination of CCPs in that order.

food-2-q216.prompt: After reading the textbook's cooked white rice example, a company concluded, “No heating process needs a CCP.” How should the supervisor explain?
options: If a CCP is unnecessary, eliminate general hygiene management too.
Every process with “heating” in its name must always be a CCP.
Do not generalize an example for one product; analyze the hazards and control methods for the company's own product before deciding.
The explanation about cooked white rice is a rule for all foods, so the conclusion is correct.
food-2-q216.explanation: The textbook explains that effective general hygiene management and HACCP plans differ depending on the product.
optionExplanations: Even where general hygiene management prevents hazards, that management is still necessary.
CCPs cannot be determined by process names alone; hazard analysis and other work are needed.
The textbook explains that effective general hygiene management and HACCP plans differ depending on the product.
An explanation for one product cannot be applied uniformly to other products.

food-2-q279.prompt: After identifying hazards in new equipment, the priority of countermeasures is being considered. What assessment is needed?
options: The likelihood of injury or illness and the severity if it occurs.
Only the equipment's purchase price.
Only how new the workbench looks.
Only workers' years of service.
food-2-q279.explanation: Estimate risk using factors such as likelihood and severity, then set priorities for countermeasures.
optionExplanations: Estimate risk using factors such as likelihood and severity, then set priorities for countermeasures.
Price alone cannot assess the extent of harm to people.
Appearance alone does not assess risk.
Experience alone cannot assess hazards or the extent of harm.

food-2-q195.prompt: Old and new work instructions are posted side by side, and workers have been referring to the old version. Which procedural and organizational measure appropriately prevents errors?
options: Keep both versions visible and rely only on individuals' memory.
Leave the postings unchanged and give only new workers additional tests.
Keep adding new instructions while leaving old versions in the same place.
Organize work procedures and signs so that the required steps are clear.
food-2-q195.explanation: Procedural and organizational measures prevent mistakes by reviewing work procedures and on-site signs to make them easy to understand.
optionExplanations: The cause—confusing signs—remains.
Even if the person in charge has the knowledge, the signage problem that leads to choosing the old version remains.
This increases the mixture of information and makes the correct procedure harder to identify.
Procedural and organizational measures prevent mistakes by reviewing work procedures and on-site signs to make them easy to understand.

food-2-q084.prompt: A new worker can correctly explain a cleaning agent's properties but cannot operate the designated measuring device well. What training is mainly needed?
options: Practice operation using the actual measuring device and check the worker's skills.
Only repeat lectures requiring memorization of the cleaning agent's properties.
Scold only a lack of motivation, without investigating why the worker cannot operate it.
Assign solo work because there is a record of lecture attendance.
food-2-q084.explanation: When someone has knowledge but cannot put it into practice, skills training that teaches how to do it is needed.
optionExplanations: When someone has knowledge but cannot put it into practice, skills training that teaches how to do it is needed.
Knowledge already understood does not make up for a lack of operating skills.
Failure to master operation must not be assumed to be only an attitude problem.
Attendance records alone do not confirm the ability to operate the device.

food-2-q282.prompt: The team is sharing the quality observation “the browning is dark.” What is the most appropriate way to quantify it?
options: Judge browning by the age of the person in charge.
Replace color information with production quantity.
Let everyone evaluate it using whatever words they like.
Record the degree using the same color chart and evaluation method.
food-2-q282.explanation: A shared color chart or similar tool allows qualitative sensory information to be handled quantitatively.
optionExplanations: Age is not a measurement standard for product browning.
Production quantity does not express the degree of browning.
Unrestricted wording alone makes it difficult to align people's evaluation impressions.
A shared color chart or similar tool allows qualitative sensory information to be handled quantitatively.

food-2-q193.prompt: A new worker notices signs of danger but does not understand their meaning or the stopping and reporting procedure. Considering times when the supervisor is absent, what should safety training aim to achieve?
options: Prohibit all judgments without instructions from the supervisor.
Aim for enthusiasm to keep working even when danger is sensed.
Make memorizing many terms the sole ultimate goal.
Help the worker understand hazards and safely stop and report in accordance with authority and procedures.
food-2-q193.explanation: Develop the ability to understand the importance of safety and protect oneself. This does not mean requiring workers to make repairs on their own authority.
optionExplanations: This does not develop the worker's ability to think about safety independently.
Ignoring danger is not the ability to ensure safety.
Knowledge must also lead to safe action.
Develop the ability to understand the importance of safety and protect oneself. This does not mean requiring workers to make repairs on their own authority.

food-2-q247.prompt: An unusual product aroma has been reported. Bacterial test results are within the limits. What quality-check instruction is appropriate?
options: Change the bacterial count record to a failure solely because the aroma is unusual.
Do not check the aroma because the bacterial test passed.
Check the specified quality attributes, including sensory inspection, and have the manager make the judgment.
Leave the shipping decision solely to the worker who made the report.
food-2-q247.explanation: Food inspection includes sensory inspection such as smell, and managers evaluate the results.
optionExplanations: Results of a different test must not be changed to something contrary to the facts.
Bacterial testing alone cannot determine every aspect of food quality.
Food inspection includes sensory inspection such as smell, and managers evaluate the results.
Decisions such as shipping must follow the specified management responsibilities.

food-2-q246.prompt: The timer for inspection has not been calibrated. A designated, calibrated timer is nearby. What instruction should be given before starting the inspection?
options: Prioritize the uncalibrated timer because it looks newer.
Switch to the designated calibrated timer, check it, and then inspect.
Substitute the timekeeper's sense of time.
Do not distinguish between the timers because both displays are running.
food-2-q246.explanation: Time is also an important quality factor, so use the designated calibrated equipment.
optionExplanations: Newness does not replace calibration or confirmation of the required accuracy.
Time is also an important quality factor, so use the designated calibrated equipment.
A sense of time cannot meet the specified accuracy and procedure.
A running display alone does not confirm measurement accuracy.

food-2-q296.prompt: You want to assess skill items on a common scale and see the team's strengths and weaknesses all at once. Which display is suitable?
options: A list of stopping times only.
A radar chart with the items as axes.
A control chart of product weights only.
A raw material receipt and issue slip.
food-2-q296.explanation: A radar chart helps view multiple characteristics simultaneously and compare their features.
optionExplanations: A list of stopping times cannot compare strengths and weaknesses across skill items.
A radar chart helps view multiple characteristics simultaneously and compare their features.
A weight control chart cannot show the overall picture of skill items.
Receipt and issue slips are not intended for multidimensional skill assessment.

food-2-q311.prompt: The line's production output is good, but insufficient support for inspection and equipment maintenance causes delays across the factory. What should the supervisor understand?
options: Eliminating all support departments will always improve things.
The line's figures alone prove the whole factory's efficiency.
Support department functions are also needed for overall factory efficiency; work together to identify issues.
Support departments have no effect at all on manufacturing.
food-2-q311.explanation: The entire factory can run smoothly only when support departments such as inspection and maintenance also function properly.
optionExplanations: Losing necessary functions may harm operations and quality.
Local indicators alone cannot establish the state of the entire factory.
The entire factory can run smoothly only when support departments such as inspection and maintenance also function properly.
Support departments perform important functions that support manufacturing.

food-2-q213.prompt: Training for a team handling clean products ends with preparations for entering the room. What hygiene management perspective should be added?
options: Do not check changes in health if an entry record exists.
Teach that touching anything after entry cannot cause recontamination.
Treat the hygiene of people using shared areas as solely another department's problem.
Consider pathways by which people introduce hazards, including contact during work and in shared areas.
food-2-q213.explanation: Worker hygiene management extends beyond entry and considers people-mediated hazard pathways suited to the workplace.
optionExplanations: Entry records alone cannot replace subsequent hygiene management.
Contact after entry can also transfer contamination.
Contact between departments can also bring hazards into one's own process.
Worker hygiene management extends beyond entry and considers people-mediated hazard pathways suited to the workplace.

food-2-q121.prompt: New workers have copied the supervisor and started skipping protective preparation when entering the room briefly. How should the supervisor correct the situation?
options: Correct their own behavior, explain the purpose of the rules, and check that everyone follows them.
Continue the same shortcuts where no one can see.
Explain that supervisors are allowed to skip the preparation.
Warn only new workers without changing their own behavior.
food-2-q121.explanation: Supervisors should set an example themselves and help people understand the purpose of rules and why following them matters.
optionExplanations: Supervisors should set an example themselves and help people understand the purpose of rules and why following them matters.
Taking shortcuts out of sight is not appropriate leadership by example.
A supervisor's own shortcuts do not demonstrate to subordinates why compliance matters.
The behavior of the supervisor who serves as a role model must also change.

food-2-q321.prompt: An improvement plan schedules cause checking, a trial, and effectiveness evaluation, but no one has been assigned to evaluate effectiveness. What should the supervisor do?
options: Wait for someone who is not busy to notice by chance.
Remove the checking stage from the plan.
Specify the items to check, the person responsible, and the timing in the plan.
Assume checking will happen naturally once implementation ends.
food-2-q321.explanation: Running PDCA requires checking implementation results and making a concrete plan that leads to the next improvement.
optionExplanations: If responsibility and timing are unclear, the necessary checks may not happen.
Without checking, results cannot be reflected in improvements.
Running PDCA requires checking implementation results and making a concrete plan that leads to the next improvement.
Implementation alone cannot evaluate effectiveness or remaining issues.

food-2-q137.prompt: Scheduled observation times overlap with busy goods-receiving periods, delaying temperature checks. What action improves the reliability of records?
options: Have workers record the scheduled time as the actual time.
Discard records from delayed days and retain only compliant days.
Fill in only the values later in a batch from memory.
Retain actual observation times and review assignments and operations so that observations can be performed properly and realistically.
food-2-q137.explanation: It is important to accurately record whether observations were made at the specified times and establish feasible operations.
optionExplanations: Times that differ from reality do not reveal how monitoring was actually performed.
Hiding unfavorable records prevents verification of control conditions.
Retrospective entries from memory do not produce accurate observation records.
It is important to accurately record whether observations were made at the specified times and establish feasible operations.

food-2-q199.prompt: Mistakes in work previously performed without problems are suspected to result from declining physical function. What support should the supervisor consider in line with the cause?
options: Increase difficult tasks to build familiarity without checking the person's condition.
Understand the person's condition and consider necessary training and support from others.
Judge that current ability is unchanged based only on past performance.
Decide that the person lacks motivation and provide no support.
food-2-q199.explanation: Errors caused by declining mental and physical function require training and support from others.
optionExplanations: Simply increasing burdens that do not suit the person's condition is not appropriate support.
Errors caused by declining mental and physical function require training and support from others.
Past performance alone cannot establish current changes in function.
This assumption does not fit the suspected decline in function.

food-2-q098.prompt: For a product whose ingredients are mixed after heating, all heating records were compliant. What is the appropriate next focus of hygiene supervision?
options: Treat heated ingredients as suitable for handling at any time and temperature.
Omit worker hygiene management after heating if heating was compliant.
Also control temperatures during cooling and preparation after heating, and recontamination from people or utensils.
Manage the product after heating only once visible changes appear.
food-2-q098.explanation: Preparation after heating requires preventing microbial growth and managing worker hygiene.
optionExplanations: Temperature control after heating is also necessary.
New contamination can occur after heating.
Preparation after heating requires preventing microbial growth and managing worker hygiene.
Appearance alone cannot establish whether hazards are present.
